note: Gate 1 config v1 — every number here is spec-proposed and editable; nothing is hardcoded in the engine. Sources: RE_Development_Gate1_Spec.xlsx, Macro_Overlay_Spec.xlsx, Developer Guide (Gate 1 + Weekly Macro Snapshot). Open spec decisions ship as the spec-proposed default (incl. the mini-stress parameters pending the client's '300 bps' clarification).

checks.label: Sponsor integrity
checks.tip: Any SEC/FINRA action, felony, or undisclosed litigation fails the deal outright. Character problems don't average out against good numbers.

checks.label: Site fully entitled
checks.tip: If the land isn't zoned and approved for the planned project, the whole business plan rests on a permission nobody has granted yet.

checks.label: Loan-to-cost
checks.tip: Debt as a share of total project cost. Above the line, the equity cushion is too thin to absorb overruns or a soft exit.

checks.label: Development spread
checks.tip: Untrended yield-on-cost minus exit cap rate — the margin for building instead of buying. Below the kill line there is no reward for taking development risk. The kill line tightens as macro posture worsens.

checks.label: Hard-cost contingency
checks.tip: Budget reserve for cost overruns as a share of hard costs. Thin contingency is one of the most common ways development deals die.

checks.label: Sponsor co-invest
checks.tip: Sponsor's own cash as a share of total equity — skin in the game. Alignment below the floor means the sponsor is playing with other people's money.

checks.label: Comparable track record
checks.tip: Number of comparable projects the sponsor has actually completed. Zero comparable completions means the LP is funding a first attempt.

checks.label: Single-exit refi dependence
checks.tip: If returning capital depends entirely on one future cash-out refinancing, the deal is a bet on credit markets years from now.

checks.label: GMP contract / bonded GC
checks.tip: On large jobs, a guaranteed-maximum-price contract or bonded general contractor caps construction-cost blowouts. Above the size threshold, its absence is fatal.

checks.label: Mini-stress equity multiple
checks.tip: The only real math in Gate 1: bump hard costs (equity-funded), widen the exit cap, charge selling costs, use untrended NOI — the levered equity multiple must still clear the floor. The floor rises as macro posture worsens.

checks.label: Yield-on-cost vs benchmark
checks.tip: Stabilized untrended NOI over all-in cost, against the product-type benchmark. Specialty products (RV resorts) are held to a higher bar than multifamily.

checks.label: Exit cap vs today's market
checks.tip: Assuming you'll sell at a lower cap rate than today's market is a bet that pricing improves. It flags — the burden of proof shifts to the sponsor.

checks.label: Interest reserve coverage
checks.tip: The interest reserve should cover construction plus a lease-up buffer. A short reserve means a capital call the moment anything slips.

checks.label: Land basis share
checks.tip: Land as a share of total cost. Overpaying for land can't be built out of. RV/outdoor deals get a stricter cap because improvements are cheaper.

checks.label: Underwritten rents vs comps
checks.tip: Rents assumed above market comps must be justified. A modest premium flags once; a large premium flags double.

checks.label: Absorption vs submarket
checks.tip: Leasing up faster than the submarket's trailing record assumes this project outruns everyone else's experience.

checks.label: Profit margin on cost
checks.tip: Untrended exit value over total cost, minus one. Thin development margins leave no room between plan and reality.

checks.label: Completion guarantee
checks.tip: Someone credit-worthy should guarantee the building gets finished — a guarantor worth at least the configured share of total cost.
